seed: Why is the Dead Sea shrinking?

nodes.question: Why is the Dead Sea shrinking?
nodes.finding: The Dead Sea is shrinking due to the lowering of the water level of the Jordan River, which is the main tributary of the Dead Sea. This is caused by the diversion of water for agriculture and industry, leading to a decrease in the inflow of water into the Dead Sea. The Dead Sea's water level has been decreasing over the years, which affects its unique properties and ecosystem.

evidence.title: Dead Sea
evidence.text: The Dead Sea, also known by other names, is a landlocked salt lake bordered by Jordan to the east, the West Bank to the west and Israel to the southwest. It lies in the endorheic basin of the Jordan Rift Valley, and its main tributary is the Jordan River.
